County Of Fresno Family Court Services

Family Court Services play a crucial role in resolving disputes between family members, including divorce, child custody, child support, domestic violence, adoption, and guardianship. The County of Fresno Family Court Services is one of the leading providers of these services in California. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of the services offered by the County of Fresno Family Court Services and how they can benefit you.

Introduction

Family Court Services refer to a range of services provided by the government to help families resolve disputes through alternative methods such

as mediation, parenting classes, and support services. The purpose of these services is to provide a cost-effective and time-saving solution for families to resolve their disputes without having to go through the lengthy and often stressful process of litigation.

The County of Fresno Family Court Services is one of the leading providers of family court services in California. They offer a wide range of services, including mediation, parenting classes, domestic violence services, child support services, adoption services, and guardianship services.

History of Family Court Services

The evolution of family court services can be traced back to the early 20th century, when the first family court was established in New York. Since then, family court services have expanded to include a range of services designed to help families resolve disputes in a more efficient and less stressful manner.

The County of Fresno Family Court Services has a long history of providing high-quality family court services to the residents of Fresno County. Over the years, they have continued to expand and improve their services to better meet the needs of the community.

Services Offered By County of Fresno Family Court Services

The County of Fresno Family Court Services offers a wide range of services to help families resolve disputes, including:

  • Mediation Services: Mediation is a process where a neutral third party, known as a mediator, helps two or more parties resolve a dispute. Mediation is a less formal and less stressful alternative to litigation.
  • Parenting Classes: Parenting classes are designed to help parents learn effective parenting skills and resolve conflicts related to child custody and support.
  • Domestic Violence Services: Domestic violence services are designed to help victims of domestic violence obtain the support and protection they need.
  • Child Support Services: Child support services help parents obtain and enforce child support orders.
  • Adoption Services: Adoption services help families adopt children and provide support and resources throughout the adoption process.
  • Guardianship Services: Guardianship services help families obtain guardianship of minors and provide support and resources throughout the guardianship process.
